  - main:
    - text: CLASS 12 · FORMAL CALCULUS
    - heading "Continuity on an Interval" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Study f(x) = √(4 − x²) on the closed interval [-2.00, 2.00].
    - text: 18 min ADVANCED CONCEPT graph limits continuity
    - heading "⌘ INTERACTIVE GRAPH & INTERVAL" [level=3]
    - button "Reset interval":
      - img
      - text: Reset
    - text: Show grid
    - checkbox "Show grid" [checked]
    - complementary:
      - heading "f(x) = √(4 − x²)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Upper semicircle of radius 2
      - text: ━ f(x) = √(4 − x²) ● Closed endpoints ▰ Current interval
      - heading "Drag endpoints to change interval" [level=3]
      - text: a (left)
      - status "a (left) -2": "-2.00"
      - slider "Left endpoint": "-2"
      - text: b (right)
      - status "b (right) 2": "2.00"
      - slider "Right endpoint": "2"
    - article:
      - img "Interval continuity graph":
        - slider "Left graph endpoint"
        - slider "Right graph endpoint"
        - text: (-2.00, 0.00) (2.00, 0.00)
      - text: "Current interval: [-2.00, 2.00]"
      - button "Zoom in":
        - img
      - button "Zoom out":
        - img
      - button "Fit graph":
        - img
    - article:
      - heading "CONTINUITY CHECKLIST (CLOSED INTERVAL)" [level=3]
      - strong: ✓
      - text: 1 Continuous at every interior point f is continuous for all x in (-2.00, 2.00).
      - strong: ✓
      - text: 2 Right-continuous at the left endpoint a lim x→a⁺ f(x) = f(a) = 0.00
      - strong: ✓
      - text: 3 Left-continuous at the right endpoint b lim x→b⁻ f(x) = f(b) = 0.00
    - article:
      - heading "ENDPOINT PROBES" [level=3]
      - text: ● Left endpoint a = -2.00
      - heading "f(a) = 0.00" [level=2]
      - paragraph: lim x→a⁺ f(x) = 0.00
      - strong: Matches f(a) ✓
      - text: ● Right endpoint b = 2.00
      - heading "f(b) = 0.00" [level=2]
      - paragraph: lim x→b⁻ f(x) = 0.00
      - strong: Matches f(b) ✓
    - article:
      - heading "DOMAIN & RANGE" [level=3]
      - paragraph: "Domain: [-2, 2]"
      - paragraph: "Range: [0, 2]"
    - article:
      - heading "CONTINUITY CONCLUSION" [level=3]
      - paragraph: f(x)=√(4−x²) is continuous on [-2.00, 2.00].
      - strong: CONTINUOUS ✓
    - article:
      - heading "KEY FACT" [level=3]
      - paragraph: The function is continuous on its entire domain [-2,2]. The graph is a smooth semicircle with no breaks, jumps, or holes.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Prove f(x)=√(4−x²) is continuous on [-2,2].
      - paragraph: 1. Interior points are compositions of continuous functions.
      - paragraph: 2. The right-hand limit at -2 equals f(-2)=0.
      - paragraph: 3. The left-hand limit at 2 equals f(2)=0.
      - text: Therefore all closed-interval conditions hold.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=3]
      - paragraph: “Because the denominator is never zero, it must be continuous.”
      - paragraph: Continuity requires limits to match function values at every relevant point. Endpoints require one-sided limits.
      - strong: Always verify endpoint continuity.
